_readme: RUNTIME REGISTRY - the list of things that can actually execute an agent.
An agent is a role: a name, a mission, a SOUL.md and a set of tests.
A runtime is the program that executes it. This project keeps those two
things separate on purpose, so you can change one without touching the
other. If your runtime turns out to be bad at something, you swap the
runtime and the agent's identity, tests and place in the org stay put.
Only WORKING runtimes belong in 'runtimes' below. An agent.conf naming
anything not listed here is an error, not a silent fallback - a test run
that quietly used a different engine than you thought is worse than no run
at all. Things you intend to try go in 'planned', which is documentation,
2. add an entry here with the same <id>
3. set AGENT_RUNTIME="<id>" in the agents that should use it
Nothing else in the project changes. That is the whole point.

strengths: one model server for the whole house
no API key, no account, no bill
weaknesses: quality ceiling is set by your VRAM
one GPU is shared, so agents queue behind each other
notes: The default. The model is NOT chosen here - AGENT_MODEL_ROLE picks a
role from config/models.json and the resolver picks a model that fits
your card. This entry only says how to talk to the model server.

_comment: Candidates, in the order they are worth trying. None of these work yet.
Do not put them in an agent.conf until they are in 'runtimes' above
with a real adapter behind them.
planned.opencode: Agentic coding runtime. Good for the coder agent's real work, weak as a plain chat backend for a test sweep.
planned.hermes: General autonomous agent runtime. Candidate once there is an org to coordinate.
planned.remote-openai-compatible: Any /v1/chat/completions endpoint. This is how the free hosted tiers in config/models.json would be reached. Note that prompts then leave the machine, which is why they are gated behind AI_ALLOW_REMOTE.
